answer: Shared-channel attribution ledger. Each agent broadcasts a periodic signed heartbeat over a fixed shared medium, and the ledger records overlapping transmission slots; two identities claiming the same slot must reconcile a joint delta of timing offsets, which only a genuinely separate operator can sustain. A duplicated agent leaves a meadow of colliding timestamps that the ledger flags as one sparrow of inconsistency, forcing the attacker to run each copy on distinct physical clocks and network paths, roughly doubling per-identity infrastructure cost.
